The best explanation of a payment system I ever heard was given by somebody with no slides at all, because the projector had failed. He said one sentence and then he stopped. The sentence was: money leaves the client, sits in three places on the way, and arrives two days later. That was it. And then he said, I will tell you about any of the three places you want, in any order. What that did was extraordinary. Everybody in the room understood the shape before they heard a single detail, so every detail after that had somewhere to go. Compare that with what usually happens, which is a diagram with forty boxes on it and a presenter who starts at the top left corner. Nobody follows that. Not because it is complicated, but because the shape arrives last.

Taking questions in a second language is the part people dread, and almost all of the fear comes from one thing, which is the belief that you have to answer immediately. You do not. There are three moves that buy you as much time as you need and none of them makes you look weaker. The first is to repeat the question back in your own words, which gives you five seconds and also checks that you understood it. The second is to say which part you will answer first, when the question has two halves. And the third, and this is the one nobody uses, is to say honestly that you do not have that number, name the person who does, and say when you will come back. A director who says I do not know, Marina owns that, I will send it on Thursday sounds more senior than one who improvises. Improvising is what junior people do.

I run architecture for a mid-sized bank, and I want to say something about the word workaround, because I hear it used as an apology and it should not be. Every institution older than fifteen years is full of workarounds, and each one exists because somebody solved a real problem quickly, with what they had. The mistake is not having them. The mistake is not knowing where they are. When a supplier asks me what our architecture looks like, I do not describe the ideal picture, I describe the real one, including the two places where a person still moves a file by hand every morning. It costs me nothing to say that, and it saves both of us three months. And I will tell you what actually happens when you do it: the good suppliers relax, because now they can plan, and the weak ones change the subject.
